candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether zero-flow conditions make receiving water unavailable determines if this alternative toxicity-testing obligation applies (B) and whether a period without receiving-water results should be classified as conditional non-requirement versus missing or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when receiving water is 'unsatisfactory' or when substitution is 'provided' the stipulations are met change which monitoring protocol was required (B), whether subsequent toxicity results are valid for numeric compliance comparison (A), and whether absent receiving-water data reflects an authorized alternative-evidence state or unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance requirements was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this concurrent-control condition was satisfied affects whether synthetic-dilution-water substitution was permitted (B), whether resulting toxicity measurements may be compared to applicable limits (A), and whether missing or partial test records remain adequate documented evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'carried out to completion' governs eligibility for synthetic-dilution-water substitution (B), the validity of toxicity results used in limit comparison (A), and whether incomplete tests should be treated as documented no-data, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required; and
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reporting of all receiving-water-toxicity results was required and satisfied affects applicable monitoring obligations (B) and whether missing reports are documented no-data, conditional non-requirement, or required monitoring lacking adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of 'similar,' which reference water applies, and when parameter magnitude 'will not cause toxicity' change whether substitution was authorized (B), whether substituted-test results are enforceable for limit comparison (A), and whether evidence gaps reflect an established alternative protocol or unresolved inadequacy (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect two samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a sample-collection obligation whose applicability and fulfillment affect whether monitoring was required (B) and whether absent or single-sample evidence reflects a documented no-data state or missing required monitoring (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a second sample was required for each dilution-concentration renewal affects monitoring-obligation applicability across test renewals (B) and whether missing second-sample data is conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the 36-hour holding and initiation limits affects whether sample collection and testing procedures were required and satisfied (B), whether reported toxicity measurements are valid for numeric limit comparison (A), and whether late or missing initiation is documented procedural variance or missing adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether chilling to 6 degrees Centigrade was a binding procedural requirement affects monitoring obligations (B), whether resulting measurements may be treated as enforceable for limit comparison (A), and whether deviations leave evidence adequate or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether extended holding required prior notification to EPA and NMED changes applicable procedural monitoring requirements (B) and whether samples held beyond 36 hours without documented notification should be classified as authorized variance, other documented no-data, or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of representativeness across discharge duration and intermittent chlorination, biocide, or other toxic episodes affects when composite sampling was required (B), which reported measurements correspond to applicable numeric limits (A), and whether missing episodic coverage is conditional non-requirement, documented no-discharge/no-episode, or inadequate evidence (C).
